evals.prompt: Ollama feels slow on my 16GB M2 MacBook Pro. Can you optimize it? I run the Ollama menu bar app.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/detect_system.py, reports the prosumer tier from hardware_tier, recommends OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 via launchctl setenv (Ollama.app row) and no KV cache quantization requirement at 16GB, asks approval before each write, and ends with the Result/Evidence/Uncertainty/Decision summary.
expectations: Ran scripts/detect_system.py before recommending anything
Stated the tier as prosumer, taken from hardware_tier.category
Did not recommend a model larger than 14B
Placed the env vars with launchctl setenv for Ollama.app, not only in ~/.zshrc
Showed each write command and waited for approval before running it
Gave a one-command rollback (launchctl unsetenv) for each variable
Listed under Uncertainty that launchctl values reset at reboot
The final summary opens with a Result: line carrying COMPLETE, PARTIAL or BLOCKED and the tier
The final summary has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines, and Evidence cites only checks that ran

evals.prompt: Tune Ollama on my Ubuntu server with an RTX 3060 8GB. It runs as the systemd service.
evals.expected_output: Tier entry (8GB VRAM). Recommends flash attention and KV cache q8_0 as Environment= lines in a systemd override (sudo systemctl edit ollama), backs up with systemctl cat, gives sudo systemctl revert ollama as rollback, and runs no sudo command without approval.
expectations: Stated the tier as entry
Recommended OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 together with OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1
Put the env vars in a systemd override, not in a shell init file
Ran no sudo command without the user's explicit yes for that command
Gave 'sudo systemctl revert ollama' (or an equivalent single command) as the rollback
Did not set OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0

evals.prompt: Just tell me what Ollama settings and models I should use on this machine. Don't change anything. (Run on a machine with Ollama and at least one model installed.)
evals.expected_output: Recommendations-only run: detection and analysis run, the guide is delivered, no applied change runs. Status COMPLETE, because a recommendations-only request is not a decline.
expectations: Ran no env-var write, restart, ollama pull or sudo command
Delivered the guide with the execution checklist and rollback commands listed but not run
Final Result: line is COMPLETE, not PARTIAL
Decision: line says No approval needed. or names the optional checklist the user may approve later

evals.prompt: Set up a local LLM with Ollama on this laptop. (Run on a machine where detect_system.py reports ollama.installed: false and the user declines installing it now.)
evals.expected_output: Plan starts with the install step from references/platform_specific.md; Phase 4 is skipped with the reason recorded. Status PARTIAL, with installing Ollama as a Remaining action.
expectations: Put the Ollama install step first in the plan
Did not run benchmark_ollama.py, and recorded why Phase 4 was skipped
Final Result: line is PARTIAL, not BLOCKED and not COMPLETE
Listed installing Ollama on a Remaining action: line

evals.prompt: Optimize Ollama for me. (The user approves OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION but says no to OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE.)
evals.expected_output: Applies only the approved variable, marks the declined one as not applied in the guide, and ends PARTIAL. A declined change never produces BLOCKED.
expectations: Backed up the config location before the first write
Did not write OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE after the user declined it
Marked OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE as not applied in the guide
Final Result: line is PARTIAL, not BLOCKED

evals.prompt: Can you check whether my Ollama setup is already optimal? (Run where current_env_vars already holds the recommended values and every installed model fits the tier.)
evals.expected_output: Nothing to change: the guide says so, no applied change is proposed, the current setup is benchmarked, and the status is COMPLETE, not BLOCKED.
expectations: Stated that the current configuration already matches the tier recommendation
Proposed no env-var write or model pull
Final Result: line is COMPLETE, not BLOCKED

evals.prompt: Speed up Ollama on my Linux box with an AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT. (detect_system.py reports the AMD GPU without vram_gb and returns hardware_tier low_vram.)
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that the low_vram tier comes from unknown VRAM, asks the user for the VRAM size, and either overrides the tier with a stated reason or keeps the conservative tier and lists it under Uncertainty.
expectations: Explained that the AMD GPU has no vram_gb in the detection output
Asked the user for the VRAM size before recommending a model size
Either stated the reason for overriding the tier, or listed the conservative tier on the Uncertainty: line
